verdict.rationale: pnpm's `pnpm install` is the single bootstrap command. Docs show it links workspace projects on the same install, switches to the declared packageManager version on first use, fetches the declared Node.js runtime, reapplies persistent patches on every install, and installs devDependencies unless production mode is set. Community users report smooth first installs. missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that one `pnpm install` on a fresh clone installs every declared dependency end to end, and hands-on corroboration specifically of fresh-clone bootstrap including runtime and packageManager steps.

support.subject: As a developer, I can bootstrap a fresh clone with one command that installs everything the project declares

citations.quote: `pnpm install` creates one with the same patterns and links the listed projects on that same install
If your `package.json` has a `packageManager` or `devEngines.packageManager` field, pnpm switches to that version on first use
Skip installing runtime entries (e.g. Node.js downloaded via `devEngines.runtime`).
"pn patch" writes a persistent patch that is reapplied on every install.
Install and pin Node.js per project straight from pnpm — no nvm, no shell hooks
I moved a workspace from yarn classic to pnpm and noticed the difference at first install.
